name: Banh tieu
summary: Bánh tiêu is fried wheat dough with mashed steamed mung bean, eaten hot in the hand. Vietnam Tourism says the stalls show up on ordinary streets and in small lanes, and names none of them. Vietnam Airlines names Trần Hưng Đạo and prints 10,000–20,000 VND.
origin: Vung Tau, on Vietnam Tourism’s local-eating article.
culture: Vietnam Tourism places the stalls on ordinary streets and in small lanes, as a snack while you walk, not as a sit-down bowl.
texture: Fried wheat dough, with mashed steamed mung bean inside. Eat it hot, in the hand.
taste: Vietnam Tourism names the dough and the steamed mung bean. It does not add a sauce or a chili. Vietnam Airlines calls the mung-bean filling lightly sweet.
howToEat: Eat it hot, in the hand, while you are walking.
Vietnam Tourism does not name a lane. Eat it where you can see the dough frying. Vietnam Airlines names Trần Hưng Đạo.
Vietnam Airlines calls the shell crisp and golden and the mung-bean filling lightly sweet. It prints 10,000–20,000 VND. Vietnam Tourism printed no price.
where: Small lanes and ordinary streets. Vietnam Tourism does not name one street.
Trần Hưng Đạo, the street Vietnam Airlines names. A shop name is not published here. The hour is Check on arrival.
priceBand: Vietnam Airlines prints 10,000–20,000 VND. Vietnam Tourism printed no price.
